experiment: Unforced co-residency -- natural scheduler placement, same process/context, no __launch_bounds__ pinning
hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU (sm_89), 20 SMs
scope_note: SAME OS process and CUDA context as leakage_demo.cu/Phase 0, but placement is NOT forced (no __launch_bounds__, multi-block grid). Does NOT test cross-process or cross-context residue (would require CUDA MPS or reliance on default per-context driver isolation -- not attempted here, see RESULTS.md). This result must never be averaged with or substituted for the forced-co-residency Phase 0/Module 6 results.
result: Natural (unpinned, multi-block) co-residency rate = 40.0000% of listener blocks (both phases; placement is deterministic given fixed grid geometry, not scrub-dependent). Of co-resident blocks: EI = 1.000000 WITHOUT scrub, EI = 0.000000 WITH LMHC hardened scrub. This is a device- and occupancy-configuration-specific measurement (WRITER_NBLOCKS=8, LISTENER_NBLOCKS=20, 20 SMs), not a claim about production scheduling frequency on any other hardware, grid size, or shared-memory footprint.
